{"id": "3f9be45b-28ff-4f2a-afd1-768423b638ed", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "## `nebula-single-region-trail` — Visibility Gaps

The trail is actively logging (started 2026-10-21, last delivery just now), but its scope leaves several real gaps:

**1. Single-region only** — `IsMultiRegionTrail: false`, home region `us-east-1`. API activity in any other region (even from global services if misconfigured) won't be captured by this trail at all. Anything happening in `us-west-2`, `eu-west-1`, etc. is invisible.

**2. Global service events excluded** — `IncludeGlobalServiceEvents: false`. Events from global services like IAM, STS, and CloudFront aren't recorded, even though the trail lives in us-east-1 where those are normally emitted.

**3. No data events** — `DataResources: []`. Only management (control-plane) events are captured. Object-level S3 access, Lambda invocations, DynamoDB item operations, etc. are not logged — so there's no trail of who read/wrote actual data.

**4. No Insights selectors** — `HasInsightSelectors: false`. No automatic detection of unusual API call volume or error-rate spikes.

**5. Log file validation disabled** — `LogFileValidationEnabled: false`. No cryptographic integrity checking on delivered log files, so tampering wouldn't be detectable.

**6. Not an organization trail** — `IsOrganizationTrail: false`. If this account is part of an AWS Organization, activity isn't being aggregated centrally — this trail only covers this one account.

### Net effect
Today this trail only reliably captures **management-plane API calls made in us-east-1**, from regional (non-global) services. Anything in other regions, global-service activity, data-plane access, or anomalous-activity detection is a blind spot.
